hand_calculation: Gain = 1 + R2/R1. Pick R1 = 10 kΩ.
Bandwidth ≈ GBW / G = 1e+07 / 10 = 1 MHz (spec 100 kHz).
The 10 kΩ load and the R2+R1 divider also load the output.
Op-amp: two-stage CMOS (MOSFETs) on ±5 V. Compensation Cc = gm1 / (2·π·GBW) = 4.03 pF; slew 9.9 V/µs.
Stability: 100 pF load. Phase margin falls as the load capacitance rises and as the gain falls; it must stay above 45°. If it does not, lower gbw or isolate the load with a series resistor.

hand_calculation: Vout = Vref·(1 + R1/R2), Vref = 1.2 V. R2 = 100 kΩ, R1 = 175 kΩ.
At dropout (3.6 V in) the gate is at 0 V, so Vsg = 3.6 V and the PMOS is in triode with Vsd = 0.3 V.
I = KP·(W/L)·((Vsg−|Vt|)·Vsd − Vsd²/2) → W = 3.64 mm (1.5× margin on 100 mA).
Goal: the smallest pass device that still meets dropout.
Error amplifier: two-stage CMOS op-amp (MOSFETs) running from the input, GBW 10 MHz, so it loses headroom as the input falls.

Stability: the amplifier's pole and the 1 µF output pole are both below crossover, which alone leaves almost no phase margin. A zero fixes it: Rz in series with Cout. Pass-device gm = √(2·KP·W/L·I) = 0.191 S, β = Vref/Vout = 0.364.
Crossover fc = GBW·gm·β·Rz and zero fz = 1/(2π·Rz·Cout). Put fc = 3·fz: Rz = √(3 / (2π·Cout·GBW·gm·β)) = 830 mΩ, fc ≈ 575 kHz. A capacitor whose ESR is this value does the same job.
Load step 10 mA → 100 mA: the output may move at most 3% (99 mV).

hand_calculation: Duty D = (Vout + Vd) / (Vin + Vd) = 0.435 (Vd = 0.4 V diode); the controller finds it, this only sizes L.
Ripple current ΔI = 30% of Iout = 300 mA.
L = (Vin − Vout)·D / (fsw·ΔI) = 20.3 µH.
C = ΔI / (8·fsw·0.8·ΔV) / (0.8·0.95) = 2.47 µF: 50 mV ripple with 20% margin for the switch's real edges, still met with the inductor 20% and the capacitor 5% low.
Feedback divider: Vout = Vref·(1 + R1/R2), Vref = 1.2 V, R2 = 10 kΩ, R1 = 31.7 kΩ.
Controller: integrator (R1, CI) → comparator against a 0.5–2.5 V ramp → switch gate. Modulator gain Vin / Vramp = 6.
LC corner f0 = 22.5 kHz, Q = 1.7. Crossover fc = f0/10 = 2.25 kHz: CI = Vin / (Vramp·R1·2π·fc) = 13.4 nF. Phase margin ≈ 90°; gain margin at the LC peak ≈ 15 dB.
Simulate 1.11 ms and measure the last 200 µs.
Switch: P-channel power MOSFET (50 mΩ, 1 nF gate), driven straight from the comparator's push-pull output stage (0 V = on, Vin = off).
